info.title: API.SH: Google Flights
info.description: The Google Flights API from API.SH: public Google Flights data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Google Flights place suggestions for what a user typed: cities, airports, regions and stations with their IATA codes and kgmids, and each city's airports with their distance.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-flights-autocomplete

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What the user typed, e.g. lond.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The lowest fare Google Flights shows for each departure day in a range: one-way, or round trips of a fixed length (`trip_length`). Give a `month` (YYYY-MM) or `start_date`/`end_date` (default: the next 30 days; up to 300 days). Returns every day with its price (and return date for round trips), the cheapest and most expensive day and the median price. Prices are for all passengers together.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-flights-calendar

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Departure airport or city: 3-letter IATA code; several comma separated (e.g. `JFK,EWR`).

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Arrival airport or city: 3-letter IATA code; several comma separated.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: A month to show, YYYY-MM (instead of start_date/end_date).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Last departure day, YYYY-MM-DD (default 30 days after start_date).

parameters.name: trip_length
parameters.description: Round trip: days between departure and return (1-60). Omit for one-way fares.

parameters.name: stops
parameters.description: At most this many stops: any (default), nonstop, 1, 2.

parameters.name: airlines
parameters.description: Only these airlines: 2-letter IATA airline codes, comma separated (e.g. `UA,DL`).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country whose point of sale prices are shown (default US).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Lowest fare Google Flights shows for each departure day (round trips: for the given trip length), for all passengers together; null where Go…

get.description:
Google Flights Explore from an origin: destinations with the cheapest round trip found for a one-week trip in the next six months: dates, price, airline, stops, flight time, destination airport, coordinates and image, cheapest first. `from` is an airport code (AUS), a city kgmid (/m/0vzm) or a place name.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-flights-deals

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Origin: airport code, city kgmid or place name.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Return flights for a chosen outbound
get.description:
The return flights Google Flights offers after an outbound flight is chosen (pass a flight's `select` from /google-flights/v1/search or this route). Prices are for the whole round trip. Each flight has price, stops, airline, departure and arrival airport, date and time, duration, layovers, emissions against the route's typical emissions and every segment (airports, times, carrier and flight number, aircraft, legroom, codeshares), plus `select`, the value that picks it.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-flights-return

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Outbound departure airport or city code.

parameters.name: outbound
parameters.description: The chosen outbound flight's select value (segments separated by |).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Prices are for the whole round trip with the chosen outbound.

get.description:
The flights embedded in the search page. Google loads more only on a click, so `next_cursor` is null. Passengers (adults, children, infants_in_seat, infants_on_lap), cabin, stops, airlines and alliance search for exactly that trip (origin and destination must then be airport or city codes); prices are the total for all passengers. max_price, max_duration, departure_window, arrival_window and sort filter and order the returned results. Also returns price_insight.level (low, typical or high, when shown) and applied_filters. Each flight carries `select` and its segments when the page gives them; pass `select` to /google-flights/v1/return for the return flights of a round trip. When Google Flights has no flights for the search (no service on those dates, or an airport code that is not the one meant), the answer is `flights: []` with `no_results: true`, `route_airports` (the airports Google read, with city and country), and the `suggested_dates` and `nearby_airports` Google offers instead.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 3 credits per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/google-flights-search

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: Return date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a round trip.

parameters.name: infants_on_lap
parameters.description: Infants on an adult's lap, 0-8 (at most one per adult).

parameters.name: stops
parameters.description: any; nonstop; 1 = at most one stop; 2 = at most two stops.

parameters.name: airlines
parameters.description: Only these airlines: 2-character airline codes, comma separated (e.g. DL,AA), up to 10.

parameters.name: max_price
parameters.description: Only results at or below this price (whole amount in the chosen currency).

parameters.name: max_duration
parameters.description: Only results with a total duration up to this many hours (e.g. 8 or 7.5).

parameters.name: departure_window
parameters.description: Only results departing between these hours, local time, as start-end (e.g. 6-12).

parameters.name: arrival_window
parameters.description: Only results arriving between these hours, local time, as start-end (e.g. 14-22).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order of results (best = the site's own order, the default).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
